thread.title: Tech Today: Qualcomm, Broadcom Fall, Defending Apple, Netflix Shines - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Qualcomm, Broadcom Fall, Defending Apple, Netflix Shines - Barron's
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
Qualcomm and Broadcom falling together
Shares of Qualcomm ( QCOM ) are down 73 cents, or 1%, at $64.01, and Broadcom ( AVGO ) is down the the 71 cents at $250.16, after the U.S. government’s CFIUS organization decided to investigate Broadcom’s hostile bid for Qualcomm, delaying a planned shareholder meeting tomorrow for up to 30 days.
Qualcomm and Broadcom traded barbs over this latest development.
Responding this morning, Amit Daryanani with RBC Capital reiterates a “Top Pick” rating on Broadcom, writing that he thinks there is "increasing probability that QCOM will remain as an independent company .” He thinks Broadcom "has the ability to sustain double-digit growth with or without QCOM."
Daryanani also offers that new targets for Broadcom could be Xilinx ( XLNX ), Analog Devices ( ADI ), Maxim Integrated Products ( MXIM ), or Marvell Technology Group ( MRVL ).
Warming up to Teradata
Shares of big data firm Teradata ( TDC ) are up $1.99, or 5%, at $41.17, after Zane Chrane of Bernstein this morning raised his rating on the shares to Market Perform from Underperform, writing that he sees three things that are “emerging” that “suggest an increasingly positive outlook.” They are the increase rate of growth of the company’s “annualized recurring revenue,” the expansion that is possible in its profit margins, and the promise of stock buybacks from cash repatriation.
Chrane raises his price target on Teradata to $39 from $33.
Defending iPhone
Apple ( AAPL ) stock is up $1.12, or 0.6%, at $177.33, following a couple of positive notes this morning. Piper Jaffray ’s Michael Olson writes that his survey of 1,500 people who own an iPhone but didn’t buy a new one recently, suggests Apple will entice them later this year with models that offer lower prices and larger screen sizes.
And R. W. Baird ’s William Power writes that his survey’s find 15% of respondents claim they plan to purchase a smartphone in the next three months, similar to August, but down from 20% levels in past years,” though Apple is taking share , as "roughly 60% plan to purchase an iPhone, consistent with August and above 50% levels in past years."
In other Apple news, And RBC’s Daryanani, who covers Apple, and rates its shares Outperform, has been plowing through last week’s filing for public offering by music competitor Spotify . He’s encouraged by the 159 billion users from which the company derives ad dollars, even though ads are just 10% of Spotify’s revenue.
He concludes there’s opportunity for Apple there: “Similar amount of data available to AAPL would carry even higher monetizing potential (high disposable income of iOS users)."
Bully for Hadoop
Rosenblatt ’s Marshall Senk today pounds the table for Hadoop distributor Hortonworksb ( HDP ), noting the stock has been weak since the company’s February 7th report. Although that report seemed to indicate “tepid” revenue growth, he advises investors to bear in mind that the company’s switch to the “ASC 606” accounting rule, plus Hortonworks’s history of “conservative guidance” mean you should look past the worries.
Hortonworks stock today is up 32 cents, or 1.7%, at $19.06.
Netflix’s moat
Shares of Netflix ( NFLX ) are up $10.52, or 3.5%, at $311.58, following two positive notes this morning. UBS’s Eric Sheridan reiterates a Buy rating and raises his price target to $345 from $290, cheering the company’s continued investment in original content as boosting its “competitive moat.”
And Macquarie ’s Tim Nollen reiterates a Buy and raising his target to $330 from $275, after concluding the company could see average revenue per user rise as more people trade up to a “4K” streaming plan from the normal plan, shift from $10 to $14 per month.
Upgrading MIcrochip
Analysts are still pondering the announcement last week Microchip Technology ( MCHP ) will buy fellow chip maker Microsemi ( MSCC ). Mizuho ’s VIjay Rakesh today raises his rating on Microchip to Buy from Neutral, and assigns a $110 price target, after concluding the combined companies can make $7 to $8 per share in EPS come 2019 to 2020.
He sees little strategic value in the combo, but it does give the company "market breadth and operating leverage,” helping the company expand within “defense, aerospace, and data center markets."
Microchip shares are up $2.88, or 3%, at $94.17.
